q: The motion of an object in both the x and y directions simultaneously is called _____ motion.
e: The object is free to change x and y at the same time. The motion of an object in both the x and y directions simultaneously is called two-dimensional motion. Do not trade two-dimensional for one-dimensional or three-dimensional.

q: In two-dimensional motion, the displacement vector from point P to Q is denoted as _____ .
e: The change of position from P to Q is the displacement vector Δr. In two-dimensional motion, the displacement vector from point P to Q is denoted as Δr. A_r or r is a different relation from Δr.

q: The magnitude of the displacement vector $\Delta \vec{r}$ is given by _____ .
e: The size of Δr is the Pythagorean root of Δx² plus Δy². You do not add Δx and Δy raw, and you do not subtract the squares. The magnitude of the displacement vector Δr is given by √((Δx)² + (Δy)²). Δx + Δy or (Δx)/(Δy) is a different relation from √((Δx)² + (Δy)²).

q: The direction of the displacement vector $\Delta \vec{r}$ is found using _____ .
e: The direction angle uses opposite over adjacent: tan θ = Δy/Δx. The direction of the displacement vector Δr is found using tan θ = (Δy)/(Δx). tan θ = (Δx)/(Δy) or sin θ = (Δy)/(Δx) is a different relation from tan θ = (Δy)/(Δx).

q: An object moving with constant speed along a curved path is accelerating because _____ .
e: Velocity is a vector. On a curve the direction keeps changing, so there is acceleration even at steady speed. An object moving with constant speed along a curved path is accelerating because the direction of velocity changes. The magnitude of velocity changes or both magnitude and direction change is not this quantity.

q: The direction of the velocity of an object moving along a curved path is always _____ to its path.
e: On a curve the velocity arrow is tangent to the path, not along a radius. The direction of the velocity of an object moving along a curved path is always tangential to its path. Perpendicular or radial is not this quantity.

q: Instantaneous velocity is defined as _____ .
e: Instantaneous velocity is the limit of Δr/Δt as Δt goes to zero, which is dr/dt. Instantaneous velocity is defined as limitΔt → 0 (Δr)/(Δt). (Δr)/(Δt) or (dr)/(dt²) is a different relation from limitΔt → 0 (Δr)/(Δt).

q: Average acceleration is given by _____ .
e: Average acceleration is the change of velocity over the time interval, Δv/Δt. Average acceleration is given by (Δv)/(Δt). limitΔt → 0 (Δv)/(Δt) or v · t is a different relation from (Δv)/(Δt).

q: Instantaneous acceleration is defined as _____ .
e: Instantaneous acceleration is the limit of Δv/Δt, which is dv/dt. Instantaneous acceleration is defined as limitΔt → 0 (Δv)/(Δt). (Δv)/(Δt) or v + at is a different relation from limitΔt → 0 (Δv)/(Δt).

q: An object is accelerated whenever the velocity changes in _____ .
e: Acceleration is a change of the velocity vector: size, direction, or both. An object is accelerated whenever the velocity changes in magnitude, direction, or both. Do not trade magnitude, direction, or both for magnitude only or direction only.

q: A projectile is any object thrown into space upon which the only acting force is _____ .
e: Split the projectile into constant-vx horizontal motion and ay = −g vertical motion. A projectile is any object thrown into space upon which the only acting force is gravity. Do not trade gravity for air resistance or friction.

q: The path followed by a projectile is known as a _____ .
e: A projectile's path is called its trajectory. The path followed by a projectile is known as a trajectory. Parabola or orbit is not this quantity.

q: In projectile motion, the horizontal motion is considered to be _____ .
e: Split the projectile into constant-vx horizontal motion and ay = −g vertical motion. In projectile motion, the horizontal motion is considered to be uniform motion. Do not trade uniform motion for uniformly accelerated or free fall.

q: In projectile motion, the vertical motion is equivalent to _____ .
e: Split the projectile into constant-vx horizontal motion and ay = −g vertical motion. In projectile motion, the vertical motion is equivalent to free fall motion. Do not trade free fall motion for uniform motion or circular motion.

q: If air resistance is neglected, the horizontal component of acceleration in projectile motion is _____ .
e: With no air resistance the horizontal velocity stays constant. Acceleration is zero along x, not constant and nonzero. If air resistance is neglected, the horizontal component of acceleration in projectile motion is 0. G or -g is not this quantity.

q: The vertical component of acceleration in projectile motion is _____ .
e: Split the projectile into constant-vx horizontal motion and ay = −g vertical motion. The vertical component of acceleration in projectile motion is -g. Do not trade -g for 0 or +g.

q: The x-component of initial velocity for a projectile launched at angle $\theta$ is _____ .
e: Split the projectile into constant-vx horizontal motion and ay = −g vertical motion. The x-component of initial velocity for a projectile launched at angle θ is v_0 cos θ. v_0 sin θ or v_0 tan θ is a different relation from v_0 cos θ.

q: The y-component of initial velocity for a projectile launched at angle $\theta$ is _____ .
e: Split the projectile into constant-vx horizontal motion and ay = −g vertical motion. The y-component of initial velocity for a projectile launched at angle θ is v_0 sin θ. v_0 cos θ or v_0 / θ is a different relation from v_0 sin θ.

q: At the highest point of its trajectory, the vertical component of a projectile’s velocity is _____ .
e: A projectile's path is called its trajectory. At the highest point of its trajectory, the vertical component of a projectile’s velocity is zero. Maximum or equal to horizontal component is not this quantity.

q: The time of flight of a projectile is _____ the time taken to reach maximum height.
e: Time of flight is the whole time in the air, 2 v0 sinθ / g for landing at the same level. The time of flight of a projectile is twice the time taken to reach maximum height. Do not trade twice for equal to or half of.

q: The formula for the time of flight $T$ of a projectile is _____ .
e: Time of flight is the whole time in the air, 2 v0 sinθ / g for landing at the same level. The formula for the time of flight T of a projectile is (2 v_0 sin θ)/(g). (v_0 sin θ)/(g) or (v_0 cos θ)/(g) is a different relation from (2 v_0 sin θ)/(g).

q: The maximum height $H$ of a projectile is given by _____ .
e: Maximum height uses only the vertical launch component: H = (v0 sinθ)² / 2g. The maximum height H of a projectile is given by ((v_0 sin θ)²)/(2g). (v_0² sin 2θ)/(g) or (v_0 cos θ)/(2g) is a different relation from ((v_0 sin θ)²)/(2g).

q: The horizontal range $R$ of a projectile is given by _____ .
e: Range on level ground is v0² sin 2θ / g, largest at 45°. The horizontal range R of a projectile is given by (v_0² sin 2θ)/(g). ((v_0 sin θ)²)/(2g) or v_0 cos θ · t is a different relation from (v_0² sin 2θ)/(g).

q: For a projectile thrown horizontally, the initial vertical velocity is _____ .
e: Split the projectile into constant-vx horizontal motion and ay = −g vertical motion. For a projectile thrown horizontally, the initial vertical velocity is 0. Do not trade 0 for v_0 or -gt.

q: In horizontal projection, the vertical displacement after time $t$ is _____ .
e: In horizontal projection, the vertical displacement after time t is y = -(1)/(2) g t². y = v_0 t or y = (1)/(2) g t² is a different relation from y = -(1)/(2) g t².

q: Why is the horizontal motion of a projectile taken as uniform motion?
a: Because acceleration due to gravity acts horizontally
Because there is no horizontal acceleration
Because air resistance increases horizontal speed
e: Split the projectile into constant-vx horizontal motion and ay = −g vertical motion. Why is the horizontal motion of a projectile taken as uniform motion? Because acceleration due to gravity acts horizontally or because air resistance increases horizontal speed is not this quantity.

q: Two-dimensional motion with one-dimensional acceleration occurs in _____ .
e: Two-dimensional motion with one-dimensional acceleration occurs in projectile motion. Do not trade projectile motion for uniform circular motion or linear motion.

q: The magnitude of the velocity of a projectile at any instant is given by _____ .
e: Split the projectile into constant-vx horizontal motion and ay = −g vertical motion. The magnitude of the velocity of a projectile at any instant is given by v = √(v_x² + v_y²). v = v_x + v_y or v = v_x v_y is a different relation from v = √(v_x² + v_y²).

q: The direction of the velocity vector of a projectile is given by _____ .
e: Split the projectile into constant-vx horizontal motion and ay = −g vertical motion. The direction of the velocity vector of a projectile is given by tan θ = (v_y)/(v_x). tan θ = (v_x)/(v_y) or sin θ = (v_y)/(v_x) is a different relation from tan θ = (v_y)/(v_x).

q: Examples of projectile motion include all of the following EXCEPT _____ .
e: Split the projectile into constant-vx horizontal motion and ay = −g vertical motion. Examples of projectile motion include all of the following EXCEPT satellite orbiting Earth. Motion of a cannon ball or water fountain is not this quantity.

q: Circular motion is a movement of an object along the circumference of a circle or rotation along a _____ .
e: In circular motion the object stays on a circle. The velocity is tangent and the centripetal acceleration points to the centre. Circular motion is a movement of an object along the circumference of a circle or rotation along a circular path. Do not trade circular path for straight line or parabolic path.

q: In circular motion, even if speed is constant, velocity is not constant because _____ .
e: In circular motion the object stays on a circle. The velocity is tangent and the centripetal acceleration points to the centre. In circular motion, even if speed is constant, velocity is not constant because direction changes continuously. Do not trade direction changes continuously for speed changes or mass changes.

q: The velocity in circular motion is also called _____ .
e: In circular motion the object stays on a circle. The velocity is tangent and the centripetal acceleration points to the centre. The velocity in circular motion is also called tangential velocity. Do not trade tangential velocity for radial velocity or angular velocity.

q: Angular displacement $\theta$ is defined as the ratio of _____ to radius.
e: Angular displacement is the angle swept, θ = s/r in radians. Angular displacement θ is defined as the ratio of arc length to radius. Chord length or diameter is not this quantity.

q: The SI unit of angular displacement is the _____ .
e: Angular displacement is the angle swept, θ = s/r in radians. The SI unit of angular displacement is the radian. Do not trade radian for degree or revolution.

q: One radian is defined as the angle subtended at the centre of a circle by an arc whose length is equal to the _____ .
e: One radian is the angle at the centre when the arc length equals the radius. One radian is defined as the angle subtended at the centre of a circle by an arc whose length is equal to the radius. Diameter or circumference is not this quantity.

q: The relation $1 \text{ rev} = 2\pi \text{ rad}$ implies that $360^{\circ}$ equals _____ .
e: The relation 1 rev = 2π rad implies that 360° equals 2π rad. π rad or (π)/(2) rad is a different relation from 2π rad.

q: Average angular velocity is the ratio of the change in angular displacement to _____ .
e: Angular displacement is the angle swept, θ = s/r in radians. Average angular velocity is the ratio of the change in angular displacement to time taken. Do not trade time taken for distance traveled or radius.

q: Instantaneous angular velocity is defined as the _____ of angular displacement.
a: first derivative with respect to time
second derivative with respect to time
e: Angular displacement is the angle swept, θ = s/r in radians. Instantaneous angular velocity is defined as the first derivative with respect to time of angular displacement. Do not trade first derivative with respect to time for second derivative with respect to time or integral over time.

q: The unit of angular velocity is NOT _____ .
e: Angular velocity is the rate of change of angular displacement, dθ/dt. The unit of angular velocity is NOT m s^-1. Rad s^-1 or rpm is not this quantity.

q: Average angular acceleration is the ratio of the change in angular velocity to _____ .
e: Angular velocity is the rate of change of angular displacement, dθ/dt. Average angular acceleration is the ratio of the change in angular velocity to time taken. Do not trade time taken for angular displacement or radius.

q: Instantaneous angular acceleration is the time rate of change of _____ .
e: Angular acceleration is the rate of change of angular velocity, dω/dt. Angular displacement or linear velocity is not this quantity.

q: The relation between tangential speed $v$ and angular speed $\omega$ is _____ .
e: Circular motion uses angle, ω, and a centre-pointing acceleration v²/r. The relation between tangential speed v and angular speed ω is v = ω r. v = ω / r or v = ω² r is a different relation from v = ω r.

q: The relation between tangential acceleration $a_t$ and angular acceleration $\alpha$ is _____ .
e: Angular acceleration is the rate of change of angular velocity, dω/dt. The relation between tangential acceleration a_t and angular acceleration α is a_t = α r. a_t = α / r or a_t = α² r is a different relation from a_t = α r.

q: In uniform circular motion, the angular acceleration is _____ .
e: In circular motion the object stays on a circle. The velocity is tangent and the centripetal acceleration points to the centre. In uniform circular motion, the angular acceleration is zero. Constant and non-zero or increasing is not this quantity.

q: Angular velocity and angular acceleration are _____ quantities.
e: Angular velocity is the rate of change of angular displacement, dθ/dt. Angular velocity and angular acceleration are vector quantities. Scalar or dimensionless is not this quantity.

q: The direction of linear (tangential) acceleration in circular motion is _____ to the path.
e: In circular motion the object stays on a circle. The velocity is tangent and the centripetal acceleration points to the centre. The direction of linear (tangential) acceleration in circular motion is tangential to the path. Radial or perpendicular is not this quantity.

q: If a disc rotates at 45 rpm, its angular speed in rad s$^{-1}$ is _____ .
e: Circular motion uses angle, ω, and a centre-pointing acceleration v²/r. If a disc rotates at 45 rpm, its angular speed in rad s^-1 is 1.5π. (π)/(2) or 3π is a different relation from 1.5π.

q: A particle rotating with uniform angular speed undergoes _____ .
e: Circular motion uses angle, ω, and a centre-pointing acceleration v²/r. A particle rotating with uniform angular speed undergoes uniform circular motion. Non-uniform circular motion or linear motion is not this quantity.

q: Which of the following is NOT a unit of angular acceleration?
e: Angular acceleration is the rate of change of angular velocity, dω/dt. Which of the following is NOT a unit of angular acceleration? Do not trade m s^-2 for rad s^-2 or rev s^-2.
